subject: Expansion: onboarding two additional projects and key orchestration
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aegishealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New projects - onboarding and API keys

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the great demo last week. We're ready to move forward with two more internal projects that need Redwood API access:

- CareNotes (team: Clinical Apps) — lightweight chat for clinician workflows
- PatientSearch (team: Data Services) — embeddings and reranking for patient lookup

Can you outline how we should handle provisioning keys for multiple projects? We want isolation between staging/prod and clear rotation policies. Also, a rough estimate of any cost uplift for adding both projects to our current Dedicated pool (we're on the Standard 4-GPU plan).

I've cc'd procurement to flag any PO/contract work. We aim to start a pilot for CareNotes the week of July 20.

Appreciate a short checklist and next steps.

Cheers,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of Integrations
Aegis Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aegishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New projects - onboarding and API keys

Tom — thanks, excited to get these two teams running. High level next steps below, plus a couple quick questions so we size the rollout: 

1) Technical provisioning and keys (Ben will handle the details): we recommend separate API keys per app + separate keys for staging/prod. That makes RBAC and rate limits straightforward and gives you clear audit trails.
2) Capacity: what peak concurrent requests / tokens per month do you expect for CareNotes and PatientSearch? If you can give ballpark QPS and average tokens per call we can recommend whether to add a Dedicated shard or rely on burst capacity.
3) Timeline: propose pilot for CareNotes (staging) week of 2026-07-20, full prod by 2026-08-10. PatientSearch pilot week of 2026-08-03.
4) Procurement / terms: if you'd like a consolidated amendment to cover both projects and a 12-month commitment for the incremental capacity, I can prepare an addendum and a DocuSign link.

Attached: rollout_playbook_v1.pdf — a short playbook with recommended env separation, orchestration steps, and a template mutual action plan.

Ben — would you propose the key naming scheme and a minimal staging/prod rate map we can share with Aegis?

Tom — once I have the QPS estimates I'll draft an amendment and a scoped cost estimate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aegishealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New projects - onboarding and API keys

Tom / Marissa — quick technical reply on key orchestration and throughput: 

- Key strategy: {account-id}.{project}.{env}.{purpose} e.g., aegis.carenotes.prod.ingest
- Staging vs Prod: strongly recommend separate key pairs and separate roles in Redwood Console. Staging keys: rate-limited to 5-10% of prod traffic.
- Rotation: rotate secrets every 90 days by default; we can enable automatic rotation tied to your KMS if needed.
- Throughput tiers (guideline incremental capacity):
  * +1 shard (4xA100 equiv) — supports ~120 QPS sustained at 2k avg tokens/call
  * Burst overlay — +20% headroom for spikes

If you expect <30 QPS per app, we can initially use burst capacity on Standard and avoid immediate Dedicated expansion. For embedding-heavy PatientSearch (if you run dense reranking at query time) plan for dedicated capacity.

I can draft a staging->prod provisioning checklist and an aead-safe key rotation snippet you can plug into CI. Also attaching a rough estimate spreadsheet (aegis_mop_estimate.xlsx).

- Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aegishealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New projects - onboarding and API keys

Thanks Ben — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- CareNotes: expected peak ~25 QPS, ~1,500 tokens/call (mostly chat). Pilot needs to support 5 clinicians concurrently initially.
- PatientSearch: embeddings + rerank. Expected peak ~12 QPS but heavy tokenization/embedding cost (avg 3k tokens per request).
- We prefer separate keys exactly as you suggested.

Procurement here — we are reviewing onboarding dates and the amendment. Two asks from finance:
1) Is Redwood willing to extend a 10% one-time onboarding credit if we sign an amendment covering both projects for 12 months?
2) Can your team provide standard SLAs in writing for Dedicated shard availability and a simple escalation contact list for incidents?

If you can send a one-pager estimate + amendment, Procurement will circulate for PO approval. Looking to finalize by July 23 to hit pilot dates.

Tom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@aegishealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New projects - onboarding and API keys

Tom / Procurement — attaching a concise amendment and estimate. Summary below: 

- Proposal: 12-month commit for incremental capacity equivalent to +1 shard dedicated (RDW-5674).
- Commercials: 10% one-time onboarding credit applied to first invoice for the committed capacity (approved by Sales).
- SLA: 99.5% Dedicated availability for committed shard; incident escalation list included in the appendix.
- Next steps: I'll send a DocuSign for the amendment and a HubSpot record for signatures.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/doc/abc123
HubSpot: https://app.redwood.com/deals/RDW-5674

If procurement approves the amendment, we'll provision staging keys immediately and schedule a technical kickoff for July 19 to prep CareNotes pilot (one week buffer to your July 20 target).

Best,
Marissa Cole
